Treatment summary
Patient persented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with reoprted head
impact and subsequent headache, dizziness, and difficulty concentrating. Over the
course of 17 visits, the patient received care consistent with standard management of
concussion, including symptom monitoring, vestibular and cognitive assessment,
graduated activity guidance, and gradual return-to-activity planning. The mechanism of
injury is consistent with the reported symptoms and the force involved in the
collision. Examination revealed some findings supportive of a concussive injury,
including mild balance deficits and reduced performance on portions of cognitive
screening, while other neurological tests, including cranial nerve function, strength,
and coordination, remained within normal limits. No prior injury to the head or neck
region is documented in the available history. Treatment frequency decreased steadily
as symptoms improved, and the patient was discharged from active care once symptoms
had largely resolved. Billed services reflect the treatment provided, with no
duplicate or repeated charges identified.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
